newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras denies phone rate hike reports.
newsitem.headline: Telebras denies phone rate hike reports.

text.p: Brazil's Telebras denied newspaper reports it planned a 200 percent hike in basic telephone subscription rates for November.
"A rate hike is planned for November but no one can say at this point what it will be," a company spokesman said.
"It is a long, complicated process and it will be the government, not Telebras, that makes the decision," he added.
Newspapers on Wednesday quoted Telebras President Francisco Xavier as saying rates for basic service would be raised from 3.74 reais to 11.22 reais by November.

The reports sparked a sharp rise in Telebras shares, with preferred stock jumping 3.5 percent to 76.80 reais to lead the Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index up 2.3 percent to 62,673 points by 1237 local/1537 gmt.
The spokesman said reporters at a congressional committee meeting Tuesday misunderstood a transparency Xavier had presented during discussions of Telebras's rate restructuring.
"It is all speculation by the papers," he said of the press reports. Xavier "did not mention any numbers," he said.
